content.text:
I reviewed the entire agreement (single section, 75 paragraphs) and searched for MFN/"no less favorable"/"favourable"/"most favored nation" language.

**Findings:** There is no MFN provision anywhere. The commercial terms (§5 Fees and Payment, p0023) simply provide for revenue sharing per Exhibit, with no obligation for AP to match or extend third-party terms to Kubient. Conversely, §1 (p0001) affirmatively preserves AP's freedom to deal with others on any terms.

input.quote: Nothing herein is intended nor shall be construed as creating an exclusive arrangement between Customer and Kubient. This Agreement will not restrict Customer offering Inventory via other agents or otherwise selling Inventory to any third parties.
input.rationale: No most-favoured-nation obligation appears anywhere in the Agreement. The only commercial terms clause (§5 Fees and Payment, p0023) provides for revenue sharing as detailed in each Exhibit and contains no requirement that Customer offer Kubient terms no less favourable than those given to third parties, nor any obligation to match third-party offers. To the contrary, §1 (p0001) expressly disclaims exclusivity and preserves Customer's right to offer Inventory via other agents or sell to third parties, which is inconsistent with any implied MFN burden on Customer. There is also no Vendor-granted MFN in Customer's favour to preserve. The preferred position (no MFN obligation on Customer) is therefore met and no redline is warranted.
